passage: On Sunday after lunch Rajni put the camp brochure beside the shop ledger on the table. “Papa, before you say anything, let me show you why this matters, and then you tell me what June really looks like at the shop.” Yusuf raised his eyebrows. Rajni explained that the camp certificate counted for the science-college forms. Yusuf turned the ledger pages slowly. “The heavy weeks are only the last ten days of the month, when new stock comes in,” he said. Rajni blinked; the picture in Rajni's head had been the whole month. “And I did not know the certificate was for admissions,” Yusuf said. Neither had expected that. They wrote both sets of dates on one sheet and agreed to check the camp calendar together on Monday.

qa.q: When are the heavy weeks at the shop?
qa.a: The last ten days of the month, when new stock comes in.

qa.q: What did Rajni feel when Yusuf described the busy weeks?
qa.a: Surprise: Rajni blinked, because the busy time was much shorter than the whole month Rajni had imagined.

qa.q: Why did asking and listening work better than guessing?
qa.a: A written comparison of the real dates let both sides check the actual needs before deciding, instead of each assuming the worst.

qa.q: How does the talk look to Yusuf?
qa.a: Yusuf learns something new, that the certificate matters for admissions, and sees Rajni asking about the shop, so he has a reason to take the camp seriously.

grounding: A student explains what the camp means, asks what the shop needs and listens, so nobody is surprised.
